subject: Biology
title: Ultrafiltration Mechanics & Net Filtration Pressure (NFP)
learningObjectives: Identify the 3 histological layers of the Malpighian body filtration barrier
Calculate Net Filtration Pressure (NFP) using GHP, BCOP, and CHP values
Define GFR, filtration fraction, and calculate daily urine output
content:
### 3.1 Malpighian Body Filtration Barrier
Ultrafiltration occurs across a 3-layer filtration membrane:

```
                        MALPIGHIAN BODY FILTRATION BARRIER
                        
    GLOMERULAR LUMEN ──► [ Fenestrated Capillary Endothelium ] (70–90 nm pores)
                                      │
                         [ Basement Membrane ] (Acellular negatively charged mesh)
                                      │
    BOWMAN'S LUMEN   ◄── [ Visceral Podocyte Filtration Slits / Slit Pores ] (25 nm)
```

- **Podocyte Microanatomy**: The visceral layer of Bowman's capsule contains specialized octopus-like epithelial cells called **Podocytes**. Their interdigitating foot processes (**Pedicels**) wrap around glomerular capillaries, creating narrow spaces called **Filtration Slits / Slit Pores ($25\text{ nm}$ wide)**.

### 3.2 Dynamics of Net Filtration Pressure (NFP)
Ultrafiltration is driven by hydrostatic and osmotic pressure gradients:

```
                           NET FILTRATION PRESSURE (NFP)
                           
       GHP (+60 mmHg)  ──► Promotes Filtration into Bowman's Capsule
       BCOP (-32 mmHg) ──► Opposes Filtration (Plasma Albumin Oncotic Pressure)
       CHP (-18 mmHg)  ──► Opposes Filtration (Capsular Hydrostatic Pressure)
       ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
       NFP = GHP - (BCOP + CHP) = 60 - (32 + 18) = +10 mmHg
```

- **Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR)**: $\mathbf{125\text{ mL/min} = 180\text{ Liters/day}}$.
- **Filtration Fraction**: $\frac{\text{GFR}}{\text{RPF}} = \frac{125\text{ mL/min}}{650\text{ mL/min}} \approx \mathbf{19\text{--}20\%}$.
- **Daily Urine Output**: Of the $180\text{ L}$ filtered daily, $>99\%$ is reabsorbed, resulting in an average daily urine output of **$1.5\text{ Liters/day}$**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Negative Charge Selectivity of Basement Membrane
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Heparan sulfate proteoglycans in the acellular basement membrane impart a strong negative electrical charge that electrostatically repels negatively charged plasma proteins (albumins), preventing proteinuria.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Impact of Ureteral Obstruction on NFP
conceptBreakdown.explanation: If an obstruction in the ureter (e.g. kidney stone) causes urine to back up, Capsular Hydrostatic Pressure (CHP) can rise from 18 mmHg to >30 mmHg. When CHP reaches 28–30 mmHg, NFP drops to zero or negative, immediately halting GFR and causing acute renal shutdown.
